descriptions.text: A Curve LlamaLend market used sDOLA (an ERC4626 yield-bearing vault) as collateral, and its controller priced that collateral from the vault's live exchange rate (convertToAssets / share price) rather than a manipulation-resistant oracle. Using Morpho flashloans of USDC and WETH, the attacker routed funds through a long chain of Curve/Yearn/DOLA-savings pools to inflate the sDOLA share price (e.g. staking large DOLA amounts into DOLA_SAVINGS and minting sDOLA), then opened a create_loan against sDOLA collateral valued at the manipulated rate to borrow far more crvUSD/DOLA than the collateral was worth. A secondary contract liquidated the resulting underwater LlamaLend positions (users_to_liquidate / liquidate) to capture value, after which the share price was unwound and flashloans repaid, netting ~$240K. Root cause: LlamaLend valued the ERC4626 sDOLA collateral using a spot/instantaneous share price that the attacker could temporarily pump within a single transaction. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xb93506af8f1a39f6a31e2d34f5f6a262c2799fef6e338640f42ab8737ed3d8a4 Analysis: https://x.com/yieldsandmore/status/2028368378457362629

On March 2, 2026, Curve Finance’s LlamaLend sDOLA/crvUSD market suffered a flash-loan + donation attack. The attacker first used a massive LLAMMA exchange to push all positions into soft liquidation, then inflated the sDOLA oracle price by 13.79% (1.189 → 1.353) via DolaSavings.stake() donation. This hard-liquidated 27 borrowers (~$10.9M debt). Attacker profited ~$240K; borrowers lost ~$822K equity (Curve DAO later proposed full compensation). Lenders and core protocol unaffected.

Curve LlamaLend’s sDOLA/crvUSD lending market on Ethereum was exploited on 2 March 2026 for approximately $240,000. The attacker manipulated an oracle linked to the sDOLA ERC4626 vault by atomically altering the vault share price via redemptions and a 'donation' stake, allowing mass borrower liquidations. The sDOLA market’s price oracle relied directly on the ERC4626 vault’s convertToAssets() spot rate, which could be sharply manipulated in a single transaction through mass redemption and donation (stake) to sDOLA, causing accurate but misleading collateral repricing and enabling hard liquidations.
